applies_why: The judge text rules on a collision between D5 and C5 after considering [CR2] G, a multi-row chain response to the Isaiah 7:14 challenge.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires -- I weighed whether 'leaving the sign's sense open' meant a chain-by-footing underdetermination (allowed) or the retired demand for a contrary stating verse (forbidden).
why: By declaring D5 UNDERDETERMINED because [CR2] G answers the rows but leaves the sign's sense open, the judge rests on the absence of a contrary stating verse rather than weighing the pressed chain and [CR2] G chain against each other by footing.
